evidence: The ordinary staged order is correct: frozen task/tests/test.sh:60-61 writes zero then installs the EXIT trap; :72-83 refuses unsupported symlinks; :104-125 starts the app with env -i/setpriv and probes HTTP; :213-227 runs gates, scores them, and conditionally runs/scores the scored suite. However, cleanup :33-40 sends only SIGTERM then executes unbounded wait "$APP_PID" before ensure_reward. The generated restart helper :152-183 similarly proceeds after five seconds even when the old process group survives and accepts HTTP from any listener without checking that the replacement remains alive. These are canonical shared-template defects, not candidate drift: independently recomputed task/template/index hashes agree for test.sh bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa, restart_mcp.py 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5, score.py 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e, and Dockerfile 72998ab8ef0e4225e63b88fccdb754943c54022e25da355035efe7f759a55fdd. Raw shared-harness/results.json independently hashes to the indexed f77ed93b2d18771474a8624c01db1bc5c02320a5776ca1561e633d68d0beaf3f. Its driver shared-harness-witness.py:12 creates a TERM-resistant HTTP server; :33-43 extracts and executes the unchanged generated helper through the real MCP; :47-65 executes the full unchanged entrypoint with only a no-provider failing rewardkit stub. Observed cleanup remained running after 12.0045 seconds with the original PID 95 answering; reward_before_forced_teardown and cleanup/reward.json contain an existing zero/no_op reward. Thus this is not an observed missing-reward P0. Observed restart returned isError=false while original PID 7 still answered, replacement PID 68 exited EADDRINUSE (restart/app-restart.log:5), and helper logged ready=1 (:21). Driver SHA256 is 44b58bdf8477e2e8992988b164f62691b15f55bc219cae791056b131cd5c72e6; UTF-16 raw run-log SHA256 is 64ef9fb6d1bb872ca54e8daf691e95a9fe9e062bfb74f2d38fd66dd22f66f2ce. These finite process observations support unsafe completion/restart; they do not establish a configured grade, provider failure behavior, Oracle score, or full-verifier duration.
counterexample: Broken-app case: a server that stores recruitment changes only in memory and ignores SIGTERM can survive the requested restart while the new process fails on the occupied port; the observed false-success MCP reply would let a browser read its unchanged memory and mistake that for persistence (inference about potential grading, not a measured app score). Conforming alternative: a product-complete server may legally retain a TERM handler or delay graceful shutdown; the public integration contract requires one Node process, HTTP readiness and durable DB_PATH data, but specifies no SIGTERM response deadline. The actual TERM-resistant listener witness shows that final cleanup then waits indefinitely even on an early CLI failure, so a conforming product can be held until the outer verifier timeout. The fixture itself proves process behavior, not completeness of a hiring application.
suggested_fix: Escalate the canonical harness defect for an authorized shared-template fix that bounds process-group termination with TERM/KILL escalation, verifies old-group exit and replacement-PID liveness before restart success, and preserves reward plus original exit status through cleanup; do not alter this task or scoring policy to hide the issue.
